name: Germany

observations.reasoning: Sourced on 2026-07-27, transversal pass over the population indicator. Population on 1 January 2025: 83577140 inhabitants, recorded as 83.577 million. Eurostat dataset demo_pjan, Population on 1 January by age and sex, read through the dissemination API on 2026-07-27, dataset last updated 2026-07-09. Total population, both sexes, all ages, which is exactly what this indicator's denominator asks for. Read as one table covering every country in the record, so no value here is derived from a neighbour: each is that country's own row. The previous value was an opening estimate produced with no source and no research.

Read on 2026-07-27 from the Werkstatistik 2024/25 of the Deutscher Bühnenverein, its 78th annual edition, freely downloadable. Genre Puppen-/Figurentheater, summary diagrams on pages 388 and 389: for Germany alone, 3 154 Aufführungen, 353 160 Besuche and 286 Inszenierungen, which is 4 per cent of German performances and 2 per cent of German visits. The year is the 2024/25 season, not a calendar year, and is recorded as 2025. Basis 'form': the Werkstatistik classes each production by genre across every reporting theatre, so this is puppetry wherever it was staged. Disputed on coverage, and the gap is large enough that the figure should never be quoted as German puppetry. The Werkstatistik counts the 441 professional theatres of Germany, Austria and Switzerland that report to the Bühnenverein — essentially the publicly funded houses and the larger private ones. Germany's independent Figurentheater scene, which is where most of the country's puppetry is made, reports to nobody and is absent. What this measures is the institutional segment. Two things worth carrying forward from the same tables. The country split is published, which is rare: the D-A-CH total is 3 178 Aufführungen against Germany's 3 154, so Austria and Switzerland together contribute 24 puppet performances among reporting theatres — a fact about who files returns rather than about Austrian puppetry. And the publication's own diagrams disagree slightly with themselves, page 341 giving 352 850 and 353 160 visits and 285 and 286 productions in two adjacent charts. The genre summary figure is the one recorded.

observations.by_venue_covers: Forty-four German producers named, summing to 3 120 Aufführungen of the headline 3 154, or 98.9 per cent. Re-extracted from the same PDF on 2026-07-27, after the first extraction was found to be wrong in three separate ways. The unit is now the headline's own: Aufführungen, not Inszenierungen, so the sum is a real check and not an incomparable quantity. The same reading gives 282 Inszenierungen of the published 286 and 346 369 Besuche of the published 353 160; the residual is four productions the author-ordered list does not carry, and it is not attributed to anybody. The list is Germany alone. Country assignment follows the Werkstatistik's own rule, stated in its introduction: the seat of the company decides, not the place of performance, so a German theatre's foreign touring stays German. The three non-German producers found in the section are Austrian — Next Liberty Graz, Salzburger Festspiele, sirene Operntheater Wien — and no Swiss producer appears at all. They sum to 24 Aufführungen, 3 Inszenierungen and 5 852 Besuche, which reproduces each of the three published D-A-CH residuals exactly (3 178 - 3 154, 289 - 286, 359 012 - 353 160). That is the check that validates both the extraction and the split. A fourth check is independent of the arithmetic: the publication states on page 13 how many theatres reported each genre, 44 in Germany and 47 across D-A-CH for Puppen-/Figurentheater, which is exactly the number of producers this list holds on each side. Two errors in the first pass are corrected here and are worth naming, because both inflate. The section lists a work once per author, so every adaptation appears twice — under the adapter, and again under NACH plus the original author — with its statistics repeated. Summing the printed lines gives 3 932 Aufführungen against a published 3 178: sixty-nine productions were being counted twice. And four entries had the previous line's statistics read into their venue name, an artefact of entries that name no director; they are gone. The earlier figure of fifty-one distinct producers, itself a correction of an earlier sixty-six, was inflated by the same two faults. The count is forty-four for Germany, forty-seven for D-A-CH. No entry carries a 'venue' because Germany has no venues_list yet. What the list is for is unchanged: it is the audited evidence base the German venues pass starts from.

observations.reasoning: Collected on 2026-07-27, Germany's own session, searched in German. Twenty-one units retained, eleven houses and ten stages, each read on a page opened at source and listed by name. The opening estimate was 22.5, which is close by accident: it was produced with no research, and the composition below is not the one it imagined. Two bases were used, because one of them cannot see what the other holds. The first is the Werkstatistik 2024/25 of the Deutscher Bühnenverein, already read for the performances observation, which names the 44 German producers of puppetry productions in the season. It is a register of who files returns to an association, and it errs in both directions: it carries drama houses that staged a single puppetry production and no puppetry unit — Berliner Ensemble at one, Salzburger Festspiele at one — and it misses publicly funded puppet houses that report to nobody. The second base is the German list of publicly borne repertory theatres, whose Sparten column marks puppetry, plus the list of standing figure theatres; both are candidate generators only, and every candidate was then verified at its own source. The second base earned its place: marotte in Karlsruhe, funded by the city and by Baden-Württemberg, playing some 300 performances a year in a stage it has held since 1987, is absent from the Werkstatistik entirely. What decides a case is the denominator as the ruling of 2026-07-27 left it: a permanent puppetry unit with a venue of its own and the backing of a public authority. Ownership does not decide. Six of the eleven houses are private in form — associations, a family theatre, a non-profit — and they count because a public authority stands behind them: Waidspeicher and Theater des Lachens on Land and city funding, Westflügel on institutional funding from Leipzig since 2011, FITZ on permanent support from Stuttgart, marotte on city and Land funding, the Augsburger Puppenkiste on the Bavarian programme for non-state theatres, 187 000 euro of fixed-amount financing read in the report of its own lawsuit against the Freistaat over a further 112 800. Two of the eleven houses hold no permanent ensemble and are counted anyway: Schaubude Berlin and Figurentheater Osnabrück are production and guest houses whose whole vocation is figure theatre. That is the same reading that let France count the seven Centres nationaux de la marionnette, several of which programme and co-produce rather than hold a company. The exclusion in the denominator is aimed at a programming strand inside a larger house, not at a house that is nothing but puppetry. The ten stages are named puppetry units inside larger organisations, and this is where the German count was always going to be: Halle with nine puppeteers and two stages on the Kulturinsel under the Theater, Oper und Orchester GmbH; Meiningen with four named puppeteers inside the Junges Staatstheater; Gera with four and a puppet builder; Bautzen, where the only bicultural professional theatre in the country holds a drama ensemble and a puppetry ensemble side by side; Gelsenkirchen, where a puppetry Sparte was opened at an opera house in 2019/20 and the house itself calls that a first; Chemnitz, Dresden, Dessau, Koblenz in its twelfth puppetry season, and the Landesbühnen Sachsen with two. Under the pre-ruling wording that counted legal persons, Germany would read 11 and the east-west gap the README warns about would be reproduced rather than corrected. Recorded as disputed because 21 is a floor, and the boundary that makes it one is named rather than hidden. Everything counted here was verified today; what was set aside for want of verification is not thereby absent. Two candidates are more likely in than out and failed only on access: the Theater der Jungen Welt in Leipzig, a municipal Eigenbetrieb that reported nine puppetry productions and 119 performances to the Werkstatistik and appears among the standing figure theatres, whose own pages answered 503 and 404 today, so no named unit could be read; and the Düsseldorfer Marionetten-Theater, a non-profit with a five-strong ensemble and 124 performances in the season, whose site answered 503 and whose ongoing public backing could not be confirmed — the one municipal contribution actually read is a 100 000 euro share of a building renovation, which is not structural support. Beyond those two sits a whole population this session did not work through: the association-run figure theatres with their own venues, of which the standing-figure-theatre list alone names some sixty. marotte and Osnabrück show that the publicly funded ones among them belong in this count, and they were reached only because they are prominent. That population is the next German session, and until it is done the figure below is a lower bound. Candidates examined and rejected, so that the next pass does not re-open them: Theater der Altmark Stendal and the Schleswig-Holsteinisches Landestheater, which play puppetry with no named unit — one puppeteer is engaged at the latter; Theater und Orchester Neubrandenburg/Neustrelitz, where the puppet theatre founded in 1977 was ended by the merger of 2001 and what remains is puppetry played on rehearsal stages; the Brandenburger Theater, whose Puppenbühne is a venue and whose own programme pages name no puppetry department; Theater Naumburg, the former Kleine Bühne, a very small municipal house that became an ensemble theatre in 2009 and now plays puppetry with a mixed company, which is the case Hungary's Kolibri settled; Puppentheater Zwickau, which the public-repertory list still attributes to Theater Plauen-Zwickau while that theatre's own site lists Ballett, JUPZ!, Konzert, Musiktheater and Schauspiel and no puppetry at all; Theater Ansbach, whose Ansbacher Puppenspiele sit inside a private cultural cooperative with no public backing read; Doctor Döblingers geschmackvolles Kasperltheater and Theater Salz+Pfeffer, private houses with no public backing read; and the Puppentheater im Johanniskloster at Lahnstein, where the municipal stage hosts a series played by a private company from Koblenz, which is a programming strand exactly as the denominator describes it. Coordinates are locality-level, the city, not the street, except where the postal address is recorded beside them; no coordinate here was derived from an address rather than read.

observations.reasoning: Web check of 2026-07-27, searched in the country's own language. Two establishments retained, both read at source. First, the Ernst Busch drama school in Berlin, puppetry department, a four-year course awarding a diploma in puppetry and performing arts, founded in 1971-72. Second, the state academy of music and performing arts in Stuttgart, whose figure theatre programme was created in 1983 and is awarded at bachelor level only, in an institution explicitly state-run and funded by Baden-Wurttemberg. The German source states Stuttgart is the only conservatoire in the country offering figure theatre, which does not contradict Berlin, a drama school rather than a music school: both count. Upper bound held at 2: both courses are documented and no third appears, training in Germany being otherwise largely carried by private bodies outside the denominator. Re-examined on 2026-07-27 after the ownership ruling, which withdrew private status as a ground for exclusion. The value does not move, but the third entry had to be re-argued rather than left standing on a motive that no longer exists. The Figurentheater-Kolleg in Bochum was re-read at source. Its own site presents an Ausbildungsgang, a training course in the fundamentals of figure theatre, and names no qualification: no Hochschulabschluss, no staatlich anerkannter Abschluss, no diploma or certificate specified anywhere on the page. It sits outside state higher education, and what excludes it is that absence of a state-recognised award, not the fact that it is private. The exclusion reason moves from private to not_degree_granting. The upper bound stays at 2 for the same reason as before, but the phrase carried in the earlier reasoning, that German training is otherwise largely carried by private bodies outside the denominator, no longer holds as written: private bodies are no longer outside by construction. They are outside when they award nothing the State recognises, which is what was checked here and would have to be checked one by one elsewhere.

Its site presents an Ausbildungsgang and names no qualification, which is why it is excluded: since the ruling of 2026-07-27 private ownership is no ground, the absence of a state-recognised award is. Recorded here also because it is often mistaken for a state school, including by search engines answering queries about Austria.

venues: 21 is a floor. Two candidates failed on access alone and should be retried first — Theater der Jungen Welt Leipzig (named puppetry unit unread, site 503/404) and the Düsseldorfer Marionetten-Theater (ongoing public backing unconfirmed, site 503). Then the association-run figure theatres with their own venues, which no source enumerates with their funding: the standing-figure-theatre list names some sixty German entries, and the two reached today, marotte in Karlsruhe and Figurentheater Osnabrück, both proved to carry city and Land funding. That population is the whole of the remaining uncertainty.

performances: the Werkstatistik measures the institutional segment only. A second source is needed for the independent Figurentheater scene, which reports to nobody and is where most German puppetry is made. None was looked for.

notes field still carries the opening memory note naming Bochum and Berlin as municipal puppet theatres. Bochum's Figurentheater-Kolleg is a private school, not a municipal theatre, and Berlin's municipal puppet theatre closed. Left as written because it is the original hypothesis, not a value.
